If your father were here, he'd... he'd do the right thing.|Steph to Norm MacLean|sound=Steph Harper.ogg}} '''Stephanie "Steph" Harper''' is a resident of [[Vault 33]] {{In|FOTV}} and former pre-War [[Vault-Tec Corporation|Vault-Tec]] employee from [[Vault 31]]. She later is appointed [[overseer]] of [[Vault 32]]. ==Background== Born on February 15, 2045, Steph was a citizen of [[Canada]] and was raised Catholic by her mother, [[Joan (TV series)|Joan]]. During the [[United States annexation of Canada|annexation of Canada]] by the [[United States of America]] in the 2070s, Steph and her mother were still living in Canada; Steph was issued a provisional U.S. citizenship card on September 1, 2071, listing her as a resident of the annexed territory of Canada.{{FOTV|2|4}}: See [[:File:StephHarperID.png|this image of her ID]] (timestamp ~39:33). The issuance date can be seen more clearly in "[[The Handoff]]" at timestamp ~36:27. [[File:FoTV Steph border guard.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Steph at the Canadian border before the Great War.]] Whether concurrently or later, Steph and her mother were interned at the [[Uranium City Internment Camp]]. They eventually escaped together with other imprisoned Canadians; however, they were cornered by a [[United States Marine Corps|U.S. Marine]] in power armor. A [[Canadian rebel]] rushed the Marine with an explosive, killing the Marine and injuring Steph's mother, but leaving Steph unharmed. Joan urged Steph to leave for the border and survive through any means necessary, including killing Americans, whom Joan said should be dehumanized. Steph crossed the border, killing a [[Slit throat victim|civilian man]] for his food, as well as killing a [[border agent]] in order to cross a border checkpoint into the U.S. She eventually made her way to [[Las Vegas]], [[Nevada]], where she became a maid for the [[Lucky 38]].{{FOTV|2|7}} One night while working at the Lucky 38 in 2077, Steph was called upon to escort a drunken [[Hank MacLean]] out of [[Cooper Howard]]'s hotel room. Knowing that Cooper was the face of Vault-Tec at the time, Steph asked him how to acquire a spot in the [[Vault]]s; Cooper told her to ask Hank. That night, Steph ingratiated herself to and seduced Hank MacLean until he proposed to her at 4 a.m. The two were eventually married. Hank got Steph into [[Bud Askins]]' executive assistant training-slash-Vault experiment program [[Bud's Buds]]; he may have done so without Bud's knowledge, as Bud was seemingly confused about Steph's presence in Vault 31 over the years.''[[Fallout: Join Brain On A Roomba Inside Vault 31]]'' Steph was aware of her husband's secret ties to and work for the [[Enclave]], though it is unclear to what degree she herself was involved.{{FOTV|2|8}} During her time at Vault-Tec, Steph's demeanor would often frighten her coworkers, including [[Betty Pearson]]. As a Vault-Tec employee and member of Bud's Buds, Steph was placed into [[cryonics|cryostasis]] in [[Vault 31]]; the program involved the [[Vault 31 dweller]]s being periodically thawed out and transferred to the connected [[Vault 32|Vaults 32]] or [[Vault 33|33]] to manage their dwellers and participate in controlled breeding (eugenics) under Askins' supervision.[[Norm MacLean]]: ''"Is this where my dad's from?"''
[[Bud Askins]]: ''"You'll never find out. Oh. He's gonna find out. These are Bud's Buds. My Buds. America outsourced the survival of this country to the private sector. But it would have been insane to keep a failed nation alive. So, we kept Vault-Tec alive instead. A well-trained staff of highly supervised junior executives from my own assistant training program. Because the future of humanity comes down to one word: Management."''
({{FOTV|1|8}}) [[File:FOTV Official Trailer Still 051.png|thumb|250px|left|Steph with her best friend [[Lucy MacLean]]]] Reactivated sometime in or before 2294, Stephanie was transferred to [[Vault 33]]. By the time that Steph was awakened, Hank had been awake for decades; he had remarried, and had a family with, a woman named [[Rose MacLean|Rose]] despite him and Steph still being married. Steph eventually married Vault 33 dweller [[Bert (TV series)|Bert]] on March 17, [[Timeline#2294|2294]].{{fotv|1|1}} She is fond of Bert, though her memory of their wedding night is spoiled by Bert's lack of stamina in bed.[[Lucy MacLean]]: ''"Hmm. Feels a little tight."''
Steph Harper: ''"Won't be for long. On my wedding night, that dress got off almost as fast as Burt{{sic}} did."''
({{FOTV|1|1}}) Regardless, she developed feelings for him (perhaps spurred by his love of shoe maintenance),Steph Harper: ''"He took great care of his shoes. You know, it was one of the few things he truly loved. Get him talking about shoe maintenance, and... he'd just carry on until everyone left the room. I loved him so much. And those monsters took him away from me."''
({{FOTV|1|4}}) and by 2296, they were expecting their first child. Steph kept active during her pregnancy, participating in the Young Pipefitter's Association and keeping on top of her regular Vault duties. By 2296, Stephanie had also become best friends with Hank's daughter [[Lucy MacLean|Lucy]] -- who was technically her stepdaughter -- even though Steph was closer in age to Lucy than to her first husband by this point. The two hoped to raise their children together once Lucy was married to a dweller from [[Vault 32]] during the Triennial Trade in 2296. {{clear}} ==''Fallout'' TV series== ===Season 1=== {{Quotation|A resident of Vault 33, Steph is Lucy’s best friend. She and her husband, Bert, were married in 2294. They are currently expecting their first child, but that doesn’t stop Steph from taking part in the Young Pipefitter’s Association or any of her other Vault duties.|[[Fallout season 1 Amazon overview|''Fallout'' season 1 character description]]}} ====[[The End (episode)|The End]]==== [[File:FOTV S01E01.The.End. (5).jpg|thumb|250px|left|Steph and Bert during Lucy's wedding]] Steph helps [[Lucy MacLean]] get ready for her wedding and shows Lucy where everyone writes their names and the date of their marriage. She and Lucy discuss the upcoming marriage, and Steph expresses excitement about raising their future children. Steph and other vault dwellers accompany Lucy and Hank to the connecting entrance between Vault 33 and 32, where Lucy and [[Monty (TV series)|Monty]] first meet. [[File:FoTV Sterling Mk IV The End Steph.jpg|thumb|250px|Steph firing an SMG at the raiders]] During the raid on Vault 33, Steph's husband Bert is killed in the cornfield. Steph cradles Bert's corpse before flying into a rage at the nearest raider. She is stabbed in the right eye with a fork during that fight, but she then uses a submachine gun to kill the raider who stabbed her before firing at several others. However, she is later captured by [[Lee Moldaver]]'s men, along with [[Chet (TV series)|Chet]] and several other vault dwellers, and are held hostage when Hank and then Lucy confront them at the entrance to Vault 32. She escapes from the situation along with everyone else after Moldaver leaves with [[Hank MacLean]] and detonates a bomb at the connecting entrance between Vault 33 and 32. ====[[The Head]]==== After the Vault decides what to do about the raiders, Steph tells Norm she agrees with his proposal to execute the raiders, as she is still vengeful over Bert's death. ====[[The Ghouls]]==== [[File:FOTV_The_Ghouls_Chet_and_Steph.png|thumb|240px|Chet and Steph kiss]] Steph is shown to have recovered from the fork in her eye, with an eyepatch over her wound. She turns to [[Chet (TV series)|Chet]] for comfort after the death of her husband Bert. She goes to his apartment, gives him Bert's clothes, makes him try them on, and starts kissing him before her water breaks and she goes into labor.{{FOTV|1|4}} ====[[The Past]]==== Norm asks how Vault 31 is different. Steph replies, "What did your dad tell you?" which hints that she does not want to say anything to contradict Hank's claims. Steph claims she does not know, but says the mashed potatoes were better. ====[[The Radio]]==== While recovering from her recent childbirth by applying an ice pack, Steph receives a notification on her Pip-Boy saying that she will be reassigned to Vault 32 in a starter home unit with Chet and her baby. Norm visits Chet's unit after the assignment announcements, only to be greeted by Steph. She talks with fake sympathy about the poisoned raiders and how terrible their deaths were, but Norm does not respond. Steph excuses herself to care for her baby and also tells Chet to not take much longer talking with Norm. After some time, Steph begins calling to Chet to finish the conversation. Later, Chet, Steph, her child, and the other dwellers selected to enter Vault 32 are in the inter-Vault space, preparing to enter and resettle Vault 32. Before they leave, [[Betty Pearson]] announces that Steph has been granted the position of overseer of Vault 32. The two enter Vault 32 alongside the rest of the new Vault 32 dwellers, and the door closes behind them. {{clear}} ===Season 2=== {{Quotation|Now the Overseer for Vault 32 after the post-raider attack reassignments, Steph continues to prove she knows how to get things done. She may now be a mother, but she's not going to let something as trivial as motherhood get in the way of her responsibilities as Overseer.|[[Fallout season 2 Amazon overview|''Fallout'' season 2 character description]]}} ====[[The Innovator]]==== In Vault 32, Stephanie is still settling into her new office and new role as overseer. She is seen trying to figure out her terminal while [[Davey (TV series)|Davey]] pesters her about being confused with Vault 32's layout. Exasperated, Steph asks what Davey wants her to do, and he eventually settles on asking her to commission a feasibility study for new signage before leaving. Chet soon enters with Steph's child, asking if she will assign him a role. Steph refuses, delegating childcare responsibilities to him, though he protests that the child is not his and he is not married to her. Disgruntled, but in a measured manner, Chet points out his situation and specifically mentions that the child still doesn't have a name, mentioning that their neighbors now call the child Chet Jr. Steph, peeling and ripping apart an [[orange]] with a hunting knife, accepts the name without a second thought, but Chet tries to protest, saying that the name Chet Jr. evokes unpleasant associations with his father's death during the Vault 33 famine of 2277. Steph suddenly stabs the knife into her desk, making it clear that she's not in the mood for an argument, and Chet reluctantly agrees to the name Chet Jr. Finally, Steph asks if Chet knows how to use computers, but he says that's [[Norm MacLean|Norm]]'s specialty. Stephanie decides to send a message to Vault 31, but finds that inter-Vault communications are unavailable (soon revealed to be the result of sabotage by Norm in Vault 31). ====[[The Demon in the Snow]]==== [[File:StephHarperID.png|thumb|333x333px|Chet finding Steph's pre-war ID card]] In the inter-Vault space, Steph meets with Betty, who investigated Vault 31 following the loss of communications. Betty informs her of Bud Askins' death and the seeming abandonment of Vault 31, with Norm being nowhere in sight. While initially surprised, Steph quickly comes to view this as an opportunity to consolidate her own leadership. When Betty asks Steph to have Vault 32 send some of its water supplies to Vault 33, Steph refuses, citing the needs of her Vault and her own child. She also rebuffs Betty's point that she should be more cooperative since Betty appointed her, hinting that she has lived through much worse circumstances than Betty had in the past. In the end, she agrees to consider trading water to Vault 33 if Betty agrees to bring her Hank MacLean's pre-War keepsake box. After being told that there won't be a Vault 33 if she doesn't help, she flips Betty's previous argument and tells her that the "experiment is over" and that they have to make their own decisions since [[Vault-Tec Corporation|Vault-Tec]] won't be here to save them. Unbeknownst to either overseer, the end of their conversation was overheard by [[Woody Thomas]]. Following the Vault's guidelines to the letter, Woody meets Steph in her own apartment to report her own violation of the Vault-Tec handbook's policies (her meeting in the inter-Vault space), while Chet listens in from nearby as he folds laundry. Steph thanks Woody and claims she will "escalate" a report to investigate herself, and when Woody protests, she reinforces her authority by telling him to call her Overseer Harper. At the same time, Chet finds a secret compartment in one of Steph's drawers which contains her wallet; Chet opens it to find a pre-War U.S. temporary ID card, revealing to him that Steph is both from the pre-War world and Canadian. Steph shuts down the discussion, and Chet puts her ID back while Woody heads for the door. Chet and Woody briefly make small talk, while Steph considers the situation with a troubled look. She then forces her way between Chet and Woody to open the door and make Woody leave. Naively, Woody further asks Steph about the experiment that she mentioned to Betty, which she downplays as "overseer stuff." When the door closes, she glares at Chet, who gives her a strained smile; Steph smiles in return. ====[[The Handoff]]==== Steph's history is revealed as she and [[Joan (TV series)|her mother]] escape from the [[Uranium City Internment Camp]] in Canada. They and other Canadian prisoners are chased and fire upon, before they are cornered by a [[Vertibird (TV series)|Vertibird]] and a U.S. Marine in [[T-45 power armor (TV series)|T-45 power armor]], who threatens to shoot them if they do not return to the camp. A [[Canadian rebel|suicide bomber]] kills the soldier, although Steph's mother is mortally wounded in the explosion. She tells Steph to go south and survive by any means necessary. Including forgetting her Catholic upbringing and to kill if needed, by not thinking of them as human beings, but Americans. Steph is distraught, but manages to escape. She is seen killing a [[Slit throat victim|man]] for a can of [[Pork n' Beans]] before later crossing the border into the United States after killing a [[border agent]] who catcalled her and asked to see her passport. In a later pre-War scene in the Lucky 38, [[Cooper Howard]] is seen talking with a Lucky 38 maid about dealing with Hank MacLean, who is passed out after having been drugged by Cooper in the previous episode. Cooper gives the maid a generous tip before it is revealed that the maid is Steph, who asks Cooper about how to get into a Vault after recognizing him from Vault-Tec advertisements. Cooper tries to talk her out of trying to get into a Vault due to his distrust of Vault-Tec, but she dismisses his concerns. Defeated, Cooper tells her to ask Hank. In 2296, Chet asks Steph about the wedding between the two she has organized without his knowledge. She is short with him, telling him she is working. After Chet discovers Woody's glasses in the garbage disposal, he asks about Woody, to which Steph frustratedly claims Woody was sent to Vault 31 for a "leadership exchange program" (the same excuse previously used by Betty to cover up Norm's disappearance from Vault 33). Chet destroys the glasses shortly after, hiding his discovery. Betty finally decides to give Hank's keepsake box from Vault 33 to Steph, in return for Vault 32's water to save Vault 33. During the handover, Betty hides and reveals herself after Steph has approached the box in anticipation, congratulating her on the wedding. Steph asks if Betty has spies in Vault 32, which Betty confirms. As Steph leaves, Betty tells her she wants nothing to do with whatever Steph has planned, and that she just wants for everyone in Vault 33 to live peacefully. As Steph leaves with the box, she tells her that their deal was for the water alone. During the wedding of Steph and Chet, Chet refuses to say "I do," to Steph's surprise. Instead, he reveals to the assembled audience of dwellers that he believes that Steph killed Woody, though she pointedly warns him not to. When Davey asks for proof, Chet is unable to produce Woody's glasses due to having destroyed them, so he continues the wedding, with Steph seemingly satisfied by Chet's failure. However, Chet then reveals Steph's pre-War U.S. citizenship card which proves she is both a pre-War citizen and a Canadian, which shocks the dwellers. This triggers a flight response in Steph, seemingly bringing back her memories of escaping from the internment camp, and she runs to lock herself inside the overseer's office. Chet and the other dwellers gather outside soon after, banging on the door and demanding answers, and Steph buries her head in her hands in stress. ====[[The Strip]]==== In a flashback at [[Camp McCarran|McCarran International Airport]] in 2077, Hank and Steph announce their engagement to a stunned [[Cooper Howard|Cooper]] and [[Barb Howard]], with Hank telling them he proposed on their first meeting, which was just the previous night in the Lucky 38. Hank expresses hope that he can get Steph into [[Bud Askins]]' [[Bud's Buds|program]]. In 2296, Steph is still inside her office in Vault 32. As the Vault 32 dwellers bang on the door with chants of "death to management," Steph opens Hank's keepsake box and dons an [[Enclave]] [[Pip-Boy]] contained within. Identifying herself as Hank's wife, Steph sends a message to the Enclave to initiate Phase 2. Before apparently wiping his own memory, Hank mentions that he had hoped to see Steph again in a manner suggesting that he still has feelings for her and recalls their time together fondly despite decades having passed for Hank. ==Personality== Steph is initially shown to be a typically upbeat woman who cares about Lucy and is excited about them raising their children together. When Bert dies, she seems to fall into grief and appears to use Chet to cope with Bert's passing. Steph is seductive, as she managed to get Hank to propose to her after just hours of "talking," and Chet also falls for her very quickly. However, she is later shown to be somewhat cold after being assigned overseer of [[Vault 32]], not giving any thought to even naming her newborn child, using Chet simply for childcare and forcefully shutting down any attempts by him to protest. She is also shown to be highly vengeful and calculating, wishing death on the raiders who killed Bert. After the raiders are mysteriously killed because someone slipped rat poison into their food, Steph is not concerned at all about the occurrence. The actual culprit behind the raiders' deaths is not revealed. When Vault 33 begins to run out of water, she attempts to use it for her own gain, effectively holding the Vault hostage unless she is provided with Hank MacLean's keepsake box. Her primary goal is to survive, no matter what she has to do. This comes from having lived during the annexation of Canada and being subjected to internment and persecution by the U.S. military, as well as her mother's dying words to survive even if it means killing others and to treat Americans as tools rather than people. Steph is willing to use any means necessary for this goal. For this reason, she is cold and distant with Chet, disregarding his opinions to the point that he is unable to even speak up against her; it also causes her to completely neglect her own child and show complete apathy for the lives of the people in Vault 32, including no remorse for seemingly having killed Woody Thomas. ==Notable quotes== * {{Inline quote|Cod ham cheese and rice!|Expressing frustration at a terminal|sound=Steph Harper Codham cheese and rice.ogg|"[[The Innovator]]"}} ==Appearances== Steph Harper appears {{in|FOTV}}. She also appears in the ''[[Fallout 2d20: NPC Pack - Hollywood Heroes]]'' expansion pack for ''[[Fallout: The Roleplaying Game]]''. {{FOTV appearances |1=101 |3=103 |4=104 |5=105 |7=107 |9=201 |12=204 |15=207 |16=208 }} ==Behind the scenes== Steph was originally described as a "native resident of Vault 33" in her character description on the [[Fallout season 1 Amazon overview|Prime Video site for ''Fallout'' season 1]]. This was corrected sometime not long after the first season's release.
